key_insight: Overparameterized two-qubit quantum neural networks can “grok” after delayed training, showing epoch-wise double descent and late-stage generalization decay unless stabilized by regularization.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML practitioners, this suggests circuit depth, learning rate, and weight decay must be tuned together to reliably move variational quantum models from memorization to durable generalization.
method: Train a fully parameterized two-qubit QNN on SU(4)-complete circuits with increased depth.
Track training loss, test error, and weight-norm across epochs to detect grokking and double descent.
Add weak explicit weight-norm regularization to preserve post-grokking generalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical observations across training runs, where deeper circuits improved the chance of successful generalization and test error often rose and later recovered during training.
watch_item: The results are specific to a two-qubit, fully parameterized QNN setup, so the regularization strength and training dynamics may not transfer directly to larger or hardware-noisier quantum circuits.
paper_title: Grokking and epoch-wise double descent in quantum neural networks
